description: Chaotic signal generator running eight named attractors, each with four parameters, across X, Y and Z outputs

params.text: Sets how often a new value is generated; these attractors are not periodic, so this is a rate rather than a pitch
Attenuverter for the S. Rate CV input, -1 to +1
Sets the first of the four parameters driving the selected attractor
Attenuverter for the Chaos A CV input, -1 to +1
Sets the second of the four parameters driving the selected attractor
Attenuverter for the Chaos B CV input, -1 to +1
Sets the third of the four parameters driving the selected attractor
Attenuverter for the Chaos C CV input, -1 to +1
Sets the fourth of the four parameters driving the selected attractor
Attenuverter for the Chaos D CV input, -1 to +1
Selects the attractor: De Jong, Latoocarfian, Clifford, Tinkerbell, Lorenz, Rossler, Pickover or Fitzhugh-Nagumo
Attenuverter for the Mode CV input, -1 to +1
Fast runs the generator across its full rate range; Slow divides that rate by 100 for modulation speeds
Stepped jumps to each new value; Slewed interpolates linearly between values, which doubles as a low-pass filter at audio rates
DC passes the output as generated; AC strips any DC offset out of it
Inserts fresh random values into the attractor, restarting it when it has settled or gone silent

inputs.text: A rising edge here generates one new value, replacing the internal rate clock
A rising edge here restarts the attractor with fresh random values
Modulates the generation rate, scaled by the S. Rate attenuverter
Modulates the first attractor parameter, scaled by the Chaos A attenuverter
Modulates the second attractor parameter, scaled by the Chaos B attenuverter
Modulates the third attractor parameter, scaled by the Chaos C attenuverter
Modulates the fourth attractor parameter, scaled by the Chaos D attenuverter
Modulates the attractor selection, scaled by the Mode attenuverter

outputs.text: The attractor's third dimension, -5V to 5V; on the two-dimensional attractors it carries Out X multiplied by Out Y

notes: the Tinkerbell attractor refills itself with random values whenever all of its values reach zero, which produces bursts of periodic noise
the generation rate is set as a fraction of the patch's own sample rate, so changing the patch's sample rate changes the speed and the sound of what comes out.
